title: Pinotage
description: South Africa's own grape, a 1925 cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault, in styles from fruity to smoky and serious.
L: Pinotage gives deep-coloured wines with red and black fruit: plum, mulberry, cherry and blackberry. Many show smoky, earthy notes, and some a hint of banana or coffee. It's medium to full-bodied, with medium tannin and fairly high alcohol. It is uniquely South African.

In 1925, Professor Abraham Perold, at Stellenbosch University, crossed Pinot Noir with Cinsault, then called Hermitage in South Africa, hence the name. He hoped to combine Pinot's quality with Cinsault's robustness and yield. The first commercial wine was released in 1961. It inherited Cinsault's vigour and Pinot's red fruit.
It's a type of Pinot Noir
Cinsault was called Hermitage in South Africa
Pinot plus Hermitage, the local name for Cinsault, gave Pinotage.

Look for deep colour and ripe dark fruit with a smoky or earthy edge. Some styles show a sweet, coffee or chocolate note, from heavily toasted oak. Poorly made examples can show acetone or burnt rubber, from volatile compounds, which gave it a bad reputation in the 1990s.
Pinotage was created by crossing Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon.
Not true. Its parents are Pinot Noir and Cinsault.
Pinotage gives plum, mulberry and smoky notes
It's a 1925 cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault

Pinotage is about 7% of South Africa's vineyards. Stellenbosch is its heartland, with Paarl, Swartland and Malmesbury also important. Bush vines on dryland, without irrigation, are valued for concentration. Old Pinotage vineyards, some from the 1950s, are now prized.

Pinotage buds and ripens early, accumulating sugar fast. That's useful in warm Cape summers, but growers must pick carefully to avoid jammy fruit and high alcohol. It's vigorous and productive, so yields need control. Its thick skins give colour and resist rot.
Which describe Pinotage in the vineyard?
Pinotage accumulates sugar quickly, often reaching high alcohol.
Look for Pinotage from old bush vines in Stellenbosch or Swartland. They often show more depth and less of the burnt rubber note that hurt the grape's reputation.
Where else is Pinotage grown, in small amounts?
Small plantings exist in New Zealand, the US, Germany and Zimbabwe, but South Africa dominates.
It ripens early and needs yield control
Small plantings exist abroad, but it's essentially South African

Pinotage is made in several styles. Light and fruity, for early drinking. Coffee Pinotage, a 2000s trend, aged with heavily toasted oak for mocha and chocolate notes. Serious, structured wines from old vines, aged in French oak. And rosé, even sparkling and fortified versions.

In the 1990s, critics complained of acetone and burnt rubber smells in some Pinotage. Research linked these to isoamyl acetate and to fermentation at high temperatures, stressed yeast and over-extraction. Better vineyard work, cooler fermentations and gentle handling have greatly improved quality.
What caused the acetone notes in some 1990s Pinotage?
High fermentation temperatures and stressed yeast created volatile compounds; modern winemaking avoids them.

A Cape blend is a red blend with a significant share of Pinotage, usually 30 to 70%, with Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot or Shiraz. It gives South Africa a distinctive blend of its own, combining Pinotage's fruit with Bordeaux grapes' structure. Many Stellenbosch estates make one.
Cape blend: Pinotage plus Bordeaux grapes
A Cape blend is a red blend with a significant share of ____.
Pinotage gives Cape blends their South African identity.
Pinotage ranges from light and fruity to serious and oaked
Old faults came from winemaking, now largely fixed
Cape blends combine Pinotage with Bordeaux grapes

In South Africa, Pinotage is the wine of the braai, the national barbecue: sausages, called boerewors, lamb chops and steak. Its smoky, fruity side suits charred meat and spicy sauces. It also goes with bobotie, a lightly spiced Cape Malay minced meat dish.

Serve at 15 to 17 degrees; fruity styles can be slightly cooler. Most Pinotage is best within five years. Old-vine, structured examples can age 10 to 15 years, gaining earthy, savoury notes. Rosé Pinotage is best young and chilled.
Which dish is a classic South African partner for Pinotage?
Smoky grilled sausage suits Pinotage's fruit and smoke.
Coffee-style Pinotage is a fun match for barbecue ribs with a sweet, smoky glaze. Its mocha notes echo the char.
Most Pinotage is made for long ageing of 20 years or more.
Not true. Most is best within five years; only top examples age 10 to 15 years.
Pinotage suits the braai and bobotie
Most is best young; old-vine wines age 10 to 15 years
Pinotage's story is South African from start to finish.
